name: q_per_channel_zero_points
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI; representative overload only, chosen because it carries the mutation and return-alias contract the tests assert): aten::q_per_channel_zero_points.out(Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Registered schemas in the supplied evidence, verbatim: aten::q_per_channel_zero_points.out(Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!); aten::q_per_channel_zero_points(Tensor self) -> Tensor. This representative signature is NOT exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must never be narrowed, deleted or have its reference semantics adapted to fit this one signature. Semantics derived from the actual tests: the operator only reads metadata already stored by a per-channel quantizer and computes nothing dense. The result dtype follows the stored metadata family: the integer metadata dtypes exercised (int8, uint8, int32, int64) give an int64 result and the floating metadata dtypes exercised (float16, bfloat16, float32, float64) give a float32 result. The result length equals the number of channels along the stored axis (rank-0 operand => one channel => shape (1,); a zero-length channel axis => shape (0,)). The .out overload writes into the caller's keyword-only buffer, resizes a mismatched buffer in place (e.g. 0, 1 or 5 elements for 3 channels) keeping the same object, honours non-contiguous views by writing only the view elements (a strided out=base[::2] leaves the sentinel holes intact), and returns that same out tensor (res_ret is buf); the out dtype must match the stored metadata family, and the mismatched buffer dtypes exercised in the tests (int32, float32 and float64 against the integer scheme; int64 and float64 against the float-qparams scheme) raise RuntimeError. Overload-dependent behavior kept in pytest: the default overload aten::q_per_channel_zero_points(Tensor self) -> Tensor takes no out and returns the quantizer's stored zero-point tensor object itself (identity on every call, writable and seen by the next read), which is not a parameter alias of that signature and therefore cannot be expressed by this model; the tests also require RuntimeError for a per-tensor quantizer and RuntimeError/NotImplementedError for non-quantized input.
